## What a preregistration fixes {#what-a-preregistration-fixes .smaller}

:::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="50%"}
::: {.small}
**It fixes**

- The plan, before the data that will test it are opened
- The rule for what counts as success, before there is a result to bend it around
- A record against which a reader can check the report
:::
:::
::: {.column width="50%"}
::: {.small}
**It does not fix**

- Whether the plan is a good one
- Whether the new data measure what the old data measured
- Whether a result that differs means that the claim is wrong
:::
:::
::::

::: {.fragment .small}
A registration is a dated plan filed on a registry, such as OSF Registries or AsPredicted, which nobody can edit afterwards, its author included.
:::

::: notes
A preregistration is a plan written down before the data that will test it are opened, and the two columns matter equally. On the left, what it fixes: the plan itself, the rule for what counts as success, set before there is any result to bend it around, and a record that a reader can hold the final report against. On the right, what it cannot fix: whether the plan was a good one, whether the new waves measure what the old ones measured, and what a different result means. A badly reasoned plan stays badly reasoned once it is registered; it only acquires a date. [advance] The registration itself is filed on a registry, OSF Registries or AsPredicted for instance, and once it is filed nobody can quietly change it, its author included.
:::

## The eight questions for a replication {#the-eight-questions-for-a-replication .smaller}

::: {.small}
| AsPredicted asks | For a replication of your analysis |
|:--|:--|
| Q1 Data collected? | which later waves you hold, and which you have opened |
| Q2 Hypothesis? | the claim in one sentence, with its sign |
| Q3 Dependent variable? | the outcome of your analyst, and the rule for the new category |
| Q4 Conditions? | the predictor and its series, for the new years |
| Q5 Analyses? | the model of your analyst, unchanged, and the rule for success |
| Q6 Exclusions? | the countries, the waves, the respondents who mention nothing |
| Q7 Sample size? | the waves, and the cells or country-years that they give |
| Q8 Anything else? | what you will report whichever way the result comes out |
:::

::: notes
The short form that the course uses is the AsPredicted template, eight questions in plain language. It was written for studies that have not collected data yet, so the first question needs care in our case: the later waves exist, so the answer says which of them you have opened and which not. For a secondary-data study there is a fuller template, by van den Akker and colleagues, with a whole section on what you already know about the data, and it is in the reading. The right-hand column turns each question into a decision about your replication. Most of them you took this morning when you reproduced your analyst, so the block takes about fifteen minutes rather than an afternoon.
:::

## Hands-on 4 – A preregistration for a replication {#hands-on-4-a-preregistration-for-a-replication .smaller}

::: {.small}
1. Open the template on the page of Part 4 of your track, and copy it into your notes, or into a new section of your report if you work in the workspace
2. Answer the eight questions for a replication of the analysis that you reproduced, on the Standard waves after 2013
3. **Write it, do not run it:** no new data are opened today
:::

::: {.fragment .small}
Then type your **rule for success** in the chat, one sentence, hold it, and send it on "go".
:::

::: notes
Your turn, and this is the last task of the day. Open the page of Part 4 of your track, copy the template of eight questions, and answer them for a replication of the analysis that you reproduced this morning, on the Standard waves after 2013. Write it in your notes, or in a new section of your report if you are in the workspace. Nothing gets run: the point is to fix the plan before any new data are opened, so no new data are opened today. Fifteen minutes. [advance] Then type your rule for success, one sentence, into the chat, hold it, and send it when I say go. [go; read three or four aloud.] Compare them. If the class wrote different rules for the same replication, that is exactly the disagreement that a preregistration settles before the result is known rather than after.
:::
